# Three-Day Workshop Structure

A practical sequence that moves from installation and data readiness to forecasting, ensemble construction, evaluation, and local implementation planning.

<div class="microhub-schedule">
<div class="microhub-day">
<span class="microhub-tag">Day 1: Foundations</span>

## MicroHub orientation and data preparation

| Block | Topic | Hands-on output |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Workshop goals, forecasting hub concepts, MicroHub tour | Participants can identify tabs, settings, and output locations. |
| Late morning | Docker setup clinic | MicroHub opens locally at `localhost:3838`. |
| Afternoon | Data format and quality checks | Exercise 1 completed with uploaded CSV and visual inspection notes. |
</div>

<div class="microhub-day">
<span class="microhub-tag">Day 2: Models</span>

## Forecast generation and interpretation

| Block | Topic | Hands-on output |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Baseline models and real-time forecast settings | Exercise 2 completed with baseline forecast plots. |
| Late morning | Copycat model logic and parameter choices | Participants compare historical trajectory matching behavior. |
| Afternoon | INFLAenza and model comparison | Exercise 3 completed with notes on median forecasts and intervals. |
</div>

<div class="microhub-day">
<span class="microhub-tag">Day 3: Outputs</span>

## Ensembling, downloads, retrospective evaluation

| Block | Topic | Hands-on output |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Model ensembling and hub-ready forecast files | Exercise 4 completed with combined forecast CSV. |
| Late morning | Retrospective forecast runs and evaluation ideas | Participants understand how to test past reference weeks. |
| Afternoon | Applying MicroHub to local surveillance workflows | Action plan for local datasets, target groups, reporting cadence, and next steps. |
</div>
</div>
